label: 1D fully etched Si3N4 grating coupler, 400 nm SiN, 1.2 um pitch, 13 periods, to SSMF
core_material: Si3N4 400 nm (LPCVD on oxide on a Si wafer), grooves fully etched (half-period width), 2.25 um buried oxide to the Si substrate
notes: Fab borderline (D84b): the acknowledgment thanks two named staff of the Institute of Microelectronics, Singapore, 'for discussions and fabrication' (p.3); no other fabrication statement (the LPCVD deposition is passive, p.2 Sec. III); authors at Bell Laboratories, Alcatel-Lucent. Test structure: two identical gratings joined by a U-shaped Si3N4 waveguide, 127 um center-to-center (Fig. 3), probed with a standard V-groove SSMF assembly polished at 8 deg and index-matching oil. Smallest grating feature 0.6 um (no DUV needed, p.2). Fiber mode centred on the fourth bar from the continuous waveguide; a 1 um fiber shift costs about 0.2 dB in simulation (no 1-dB tolerance printed). The Gaussian estimate of Eq. (3) gives 95 nm 1-dB bandwidth for a generic 400 nm SiN grating (analytic, not this design; not entered). The 0.3 dB gap between measured 4.2 dB and simulated 3.9 dB is attributed tentatively to SiN propagation loss (see the waveguide row). Second-order back reflection is pushed away by the 8 deg tilt; SiN thermo-optic drift 0.02 nm/C is cited (ref. 8), not entered.

notes: Fab: 'proposed, designed, fabricated and demonstrated' (p.1) plus thanks to 'the fabrication team of the Nanophotonics Technology Center' (p.4 acknowledgment); all five authors at the Nanophotonics Technology Center, Universitat Politecnica de Valencia: org_upv (D84b borderline; NTC unit not in the registry, D533 / D553 precedent). Simulated design trends not entered: about 1 dB minimum loss without trenches (3 um cover, Fig. 2(a)); losses below 1.5 dB for fiber-SSC gaps below 20 um (Fig. 4(b), not a 1-dB tolerance); facet-distance tolerance (Fig. 3(b)). Abstract 'optical bandwidth of 60 nm across the O-band' with losses 'mostly below 3 dB' is a criterion bandwidth (no bw parameter fits; the Fig. 7 read row covers the span). SMF core diameter 8.2 um (p.2) is not an MFD (not entered). Huawei staff thanked for support (p.4).

label: Focusing-curved subwavelength grating coupler, fully etched, 220 nm SOI (non-tapered SWG)
core_material: Si 220 nm on 3 um BOX; grating of interleaved subwavelength high / low index regions (one full etch)
notes: Fab: 'The devices were fabricated at the University of Washington - Washington Nanofabrication Facility (WNF)' (p.8 acknowledgment; co-author at WNF): org_university_washington (D448, lu2015a precedent); WNF facility not in the registry (report). EBL, single full etch. Design (2D FDTD + particle swarm optimization in Lumerical): effective indices 2.79 / 1.71 (high / low region) at 1550 nm, subwavelength fill factors 0.67 / 0.13 (no parameter; grating fill factor 0.5 entered). Geometry rows are the optimized design (p.3-4); 'multiple SWGCs with parameter variations around the optimal values were fabricated' (p.5) and the paper does not say which variant Fig. 4 (and Fig. 7, tapered row) shows. Curved lines are confocal ellipses (Eq. (4)). Test pair at 127 um pitch joined by a short strip waveguide. Fabry-Perot ripples with about 1.1 nm FSR (pair cavity about 295 um) and about 18 nm FSR (front / rear curves, about 18 um) reveal back reflection (not quantified). Straight-line SWGCs with similar parameters were also fabricated; no penalty from curving, values in the authors' OFC paper (ref. 20), not entered.
